v.en: O God, come to my assistance;

r.en: O Lord, make haste to help me.

source.scope: Psalmi & antiphonæ ex Commune aut Festo

text.la: Dum esset Rex * in accúbitu suo, nardus mea dedit odórem suavitátis.
text.en: While the King sitteth at his table, * my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.

text.la: Læva eius * sub cápite meo, et déxtera illíus amplexábitur me.
text.en: His left hand is under my head, * and his right hand doth embrace me.

text.la: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Ierúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
text.en: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

text.la: Iam hiems tránsiit, * imber ábiit et recéssit: surge, amíca mea, et veni.
text.en: Lo the winter is past, * the rain is over and gone. Rise up, my love, and come away.

text.la: Speciósa * facta es et suávis in delíciis tuis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
text.en: O Holy Mother of God, thou art become beautiful * and gentle in thy gladness.

text.la: Beáta Mater * et intácta Virgo María, gloriósa Regína mundi, intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum.
text.en: O Blessed Mother, * and Virgin Mary undefiled, glorious Queen of the world, intercede for us with the Lord.

text.la: Concéde nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine: ut, qui solemnitátem beatæ Maríæ Vírginis Regínæ nostræ celebrámus; eius muníti præsídio, pacem in præsénti et glóriam in futúro cónsequi mereámur.
text.en: Grant, O Lord, we beseech Thee, to those who are celebrating this solemnity of the Blessed Virgin Mary our Queen: that safe in her protection we may deserve to enjoy present peace and future glory.
